digest.component_or_area: Jira Data Center adapter — HTTP 429 retry policy
propositions: Jira Data Center's built-in rate limiting (8.6+, DC only, off by default) returns 429 with Retry-After header, but rebar does not retry or honour the header, causing hard failures on rate-limited requests

Retry-After header must be parsed and honoured with up to 20% jitter applied, clamped to MAX_BACKOFF_S, reusing existing _errors.parse_retry_after() and _errors.MAX_BACKOFF_S rather than implementing a second parser

The 429 retry must be scoped to idempotent reads only via per-call opt-in (rate_limit_retry flag defaulting to False) to prevent reintroducing duplicate-issue failures if mutations are retried after the server begins a write

The opt-in flag must reach the retry layer through two independent paths: via _call_logged from _paged_search (PATH A) and via direct _with_connection_retry calls in per-issue fetches like get_comment_map (PATH B), because PATH A alone misses the highest-volume read

All four opted-in read call sites (get_issuelinks_map, get_comment_map's paged search, get_comment_map's per-issue fetch, get_parent_map) must pass rate_limit_retry=True, while no mutation call site may inherit the retry by omission

Cap exhaustion must raise BackendHTTPError with code==429 at the adapter boundary, never leaking the vendor JIRAError type, and the Retry-After value must be read from exc.response.headers not exc.headers
